# Deliver a work item

Advance one card as far as the evidence and the decision rules allow, then report where it stands. The
rules this procedure applies (routes, escalation triggers, packets, and stop conditions) are in the
orchestration section of `CLAUDE.md`. Read that section first if it is not already in your
context.

Input: `$ARGUMENTS`. This is a card ID, optionally followed by instructions, or a new request with no
card yet.

## 1. Establish where the card is

Run `python3 .delivery/checkpoint.py status` first. Recover an `active` or `abandoned` checkpoint according
to `rust-interruption-recovery` before selecting new work.

- **No card yet:** dispatch `rust-intake-planner` with the request. It returns a shaped record or the
  questions blocking one. Stop at commitment unless the user's instructions already commit the item.
- **A card:** read `work-items/<card-id>.md`. Identify its route, its acceptance criteria, and the last
  log entries. Take the current state from the board when you can observe it. Otherwise take it from the
  latest gate result in the log, and say which source you used.
- Check the pull policy before doing anything new (K §5.3). If another card is blocked or active, report
  it, and ask whether to finish that one first.

## 2. Pick the next stage

| Current position | Next | Agent |
|---|---|---|
| Options, or a request with no record | Shape and recommend commitment | `rust-intake-planner` |
| Ready on `full`, `discovery`, or `expedite`, with no architecture contract | Architecture contract | `rust-solution-architect` |
| Ready with a contract, or Ready on `light` | Candidate commit | `rust-implementer` |
| Development with a candidate and a passing gate | Independent review | `rust-quality-reviewer` |
| Review passed | Validation on the exact candidate | `rust-validation-engineer` |
| Validation passed | Readiness, plan, go or no-go, delivery | `rust-release-steward` |
| Rework entry in the log | The stage that owns the finding | As named in the rework entry |

Add any project route whose trigger applies (the "Project routes" table in `CLAUDE.md`).

## 3. Run the stage

1. Build the handoff packet from the record. Quote earlier findings verbatim, not paraphrased.
2. Before dispatch, create the write-ahead checkpoint with `python3 .delivery/checkpoint.py start`,
   naming the card, stage, objective, candidate, and first exact action. For a recovered checkpoint,
   confirm that its card and stage match and use `resume` instead. Require writing agents to update it
   according to `rust-interruption-recovery` while they work.
3. Dispatch the agent with the Agent tool, using its name as the subagent type.
4. Check the result packet against the files:
   - The log entry exists or is returned for the orchestrator to append.
   - `git cat-file -e <candidate>^{commit}` succeeds when a candidate exists.
   - The candidate is an ancestor of the card branch; later commits only append under
     `work-items/<card-id>.md`'s `## Log`.
   - The named artifacts exist.
   - Every claimed check names a command and an observed result.
5. Append any returned log entry verbatim with `rust-work-item-traceability`. At commitment, create the
   card's topic branch when it does not exist. Commit stage artifacts before a candidate exists. After one
   exists, commit only an append under the card record's `## Log` as evidence. Inspect the staged path and
   diff, use a `Kanban: <card-id>` trailer, and leave a clean tree.
6. Obtain the full evidence-commit ID, then run
   `python3 .delivery/checkpoint.py finish --evidence "<full evidence-commit id>"`. Never finish a
   checkpoint while the stage result is uncommitted or the tree is dirty.
7. Gate. On `pass`, continue with the next stage when no stop condition applies. On `fail`, route the
   rework with the finding IDs. On `blocked` or `needs-decision`, stop. Any non-evidence path changed
   after review or validation creates a new candidate and returns to review.

Repeat until the card reaches a stop condition, is Released, or has come back from rework on the same
finding three times.

## 4. Report

Finish with a short status:

```text
Card: <card-id> — <title> (route <route>)
Reached: <stage or state>, evidence <commit or log entry>
Stages run this session: <stage → verdict>, ...
Waiting on: <decision or event> — owner <person or role>
Next: <exact next step, or the command a person must run>
```

Never claim that a card moved on the board, or that a check passed, unless you observed it.
